bands.label: Early
bands.sentence: The work that matters still lives in people's heads. The first useful move is to write one workflow down and name who owns it.

bands.label: Forming
bands.sentence: Some of your work is written down. Name an owner and keep one source of truth, and you're ready to build.

bands.label: Ready
bands.sentence: The business can put a new system to work. The open question is which workflow to start with, and who owns it day to day.

bands.label: Running
bands.sentence: A real workflow already uses the tools. The next gain is the job that still waits on one person.

questions.prompt: If you could fix one thing by tomorrow, what would it be?

suggestions.title: Start with where the knowledge lives
suggestions.body: Right now the know-how lives in people's heads. Pick one job this week and write down where its answers come from and who keeps them current.

suggestions.title: Tighten where the knowledge lives
suggestions.body: Some of what you know is written down. Name the one source people should trust for a single job, and retire the copies that disagree with it.

suggestions.title: Start by writing the work down
suggestions.body: The steps for your most repeated job aren't written yet. Write them in the order they happen, including what you do when something goes wrong.

suggestions.title: Tighten how the work is written down
suggestions.body: The happy path is written, but the exceptions aren't. Add the two exceptions that come up most often to the same page.

suggestions.title: Start with who would own a new system
suggestions.body: Nobody has time to own a new system yet. Pick one person to own it day to day, and put it in their role before you buy anything.

suggestions.title: Tighten who owns the new system
suggestions.body: You have someone in mind. Make it official: give them the time, and tell everyone else who to ask.

suggestions.title: Start with who decides and how fast
suggestions.body: Decisions take months. Name who can say yes to a small first step, and agree a date to decide by.

suggestions.title: Tighten who decides and how fast
suggestions.body: Someone can decide, but it takes weeks. Agree in advance what a good first result looks like, so the yes comes quickly.

suggestions.title: You can put a system to work
suggestions.body: Data, process, people, and the decision are far enough along. The useful next step is one workflow, with a named owner, running this quarter.

suggestions.title: New customers come from one place
suggestions.body: When referrals are the whole pipeline, a quiet month is a quiet quarter. Write down the one other place buyers already look, and put a page there that answers their question.

suggestions.title: AI answer engines are unchecked
suggestions.body: Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google the question a buyer would ask, using your product words. Save what comes back. That is the baseline the site scan is measuring.

suggestions.title: The site cannot keep up with the work
suggestions.body: If a change takes weeks, the pages that should answer buyers stay stale. List the three pages a buyer hits first and who can publish a change to them.

suggestions.title: Still reading your site
suggestions.body: The scan is still running. Open the full scan when it finishes. The rest of this check does not wait on it.

suggestions.title: The site scan did not finish
suggestions.body: We could not read the site this time. Run the scan directly and the visibility section will fill in.

suggestions.title: Your home page doesn't say who you are
suggestions.body: The home page has no structured data, so answer engines have to guess what the business is. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: AI tools can't confirm your business details
suggestions.body: There is no Organization or LocalBusiness markup naming who you are, where you are, and how to reach you. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Your answers aren't marked up for AI
suggestions.body: The questions buyers ask are not marked up as answers a machine can quote. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: No guide file for AI tools
suggestions.body: There is no llms.txt file telling an answer engine which pages matter. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Your guide file for AI tools is empty
suggestions.body: llms.txt exists but says nothing useful. Name the pages a buyer should read. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Add a longer guide file for AI tools
suggestions.body: A short llms.txt is present. A fuller llms-full.txt gives answer engines the longer context. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: No sitemap found
suggestions.body: No sitemap was found, so crawlers have to discover pages by links alone. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Your sitemap can't be read
suggestions.body: A sitemap was found but could not be read. Publish a valid XML sitemap. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: ChatGPT is blocked from your site
suggestions.body: robots.txt blocks GPTBot, so that answer engine is told to stay out. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Some AI tools are blocked from your site
suggestions.body: robots.txt blocks one or more AI crawlers. Decide which ones you want reading the site. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Most pages don't describe themselves to AI
suggestions.body: Most pages have no structured data, so the site looks thin to a machine. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Some pages wouldn't load
suggestions.body: Some important pages could not be fetched. If a buyer cannot load them, neither can a crawler. Fix this, then run the scan again.

suggestions.title: Pages don't show where they sit in the site
suggestions.body: Pages do not say where they sit in the site, which makes the structure harder to quote. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Step-by-step pages aren't marked up
suggestions.body: Step-by-step pages are not marked as HowTo, so the steps are harder to cite. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

suggestions.title: Product pages are missing product details
suggestions.body: Product pages do not carry Product markup for price, availability, and name. Fix that page first, then rerun the scan.

offers.said: Your process is real, and off-the-shelf software does not fit it.
offers.build: A system shaped by the way you already work, including the exceptions.

offers.said: Answers wait on two or three people.
offers.build: A correct answer from knowledge you own, on text or voice, without hiring more people as questions grow.

offers.said: New people do not sound like your best people.
offers.build: The talk track, the booking, and a coach on the live book of business, so a new person sells to the standard.

offers.said: Leads arrive with no story attached.
offers.build: An assessment a person finishes, a result they can read, and a path to a conversation.

offers.said: You do not know if AI answer engines can find you.
offers.build: A scan of how readable the site is to answer engines, and the fixes that make it easy for them to read. pirx.ca went from near-zero to 398K search impressions and 46.5K AI-feature impressions in 90 days. Google Search Console, Jul 18 to Oct 17, 2026, recorded 398K search impressions and 1.94K clicks.

offers.said: Decisions wait on last month's numbers.
offers.build: The number you need while the decision is still open, from the record you already keep.

offers.said: A new channel feels like it needs a department.
offers.build: On-brand content made from what you've already approved.

offers.said: The sale still needs a visit before anyone says yes.
offers.build: Fit, price, booking, and trust on the screen, before anyone gets in a car.

offers.said: The vendor bill grows as you grow.
offers.build: Your answers and customer records, kept under your control.

offers.said: One person knows how the important thing works.
offers.build: The knowledge becomes something a customer can finish and your staff can teach.

offers.said: Fraud or order review eats someone's morning.
offers.build: Low-risk orders clear themselves. High-risk orders reach a person with the history already assembled.

offers.said: Claims drift the moment someone new writes.

copy.landingTitle: Is your business ready to put AI to work?
copy.landingDeck: A five-to-seven-minute check. You get a score and next steps for how the work runs, where new customers come from, and how readable your website is to AI answer engines, plus the stage your business is at today.
copy.consent: We'll send this report and, if you book, the notes from your session. Nothing else.
copy.bookingTitle: Book a thirty-minute working session. Bring one workflow, and leave with a plan.
